flashcards.q: What is the evaluation order for a GCP API request?
flashcards.a: Deny policies first (outrank everything, only exceptionPrincipals escape), then allow policies (one binding anywhere in the inherited org→folder→project→resource chain with a satisfied CEL condition suffices), then Principal Access Boundary eligibility, then default deny.

flashcards.q: Where does Organization Policy fit in request evaluation?
flashcards.a: Nowhere on the request path — it gates configuration writes (CREATE/UPDATE). A constraint can prevent creating a public bucket but never blocks reading an existing object.

User grants iam.serviceAccounts.actAs — attaching the SA to a resource at creation (GCP's PassRole). TokenCreator grants direct token minting (generateAccessToken/generateIdToken/signJwt) — full impersonation without launching anything; strictly more dangerous per grant.

flashcards.q: How do service-account keys compare to attached service accounts?
flashcards.a: Keys: up to 10 downloadable JSON files per SA, no default expiry, no attribution in logs — bearer credentials that equal identity theft when leaked. Attached SAs use the metadata server (169.254.169.254) to hand out ~1-hour tokens with nothing stored.

flashcards.q: Mechanics of GKE Workload Identity in one line each step?
flashcards.a: Pod uses KSA annotated iam.gke.io/gcp-service-account=<GSA>; metadata emulator intercepts token requests; STS validates because roles/iam.workloadIdentityUser is bound to principal://iam.googleapis.com/projects/N/clusters/C/namespaces/ns/sa/<ksa>; pod receives a Google token with the GSA's roles.

flashcards.q: Two independent gates in Workload Identity Federation?
flashcards.a: (1) The provider's attribute condition (CEL over mapped assertion attributes) decides who may exchange tokens at all; (2) the IAM binding's principalSet attribute selector decides which pool identities may impersonate which SA. Missing either widens trust.

flashcards.q: Why prefer repository_owner_id over repository_owner in a GitHub WIF condition?
flashcards.a: GitHub org/user names can be released and reclaimed after account deletion; numeric IDs are immutable. A mutable claim lets your trust anchor change hands without any GCP-side edit.

flashcards.q: What are the three role families and the rule of thumb?
flashcards.a: Basic (owner/editor/viewer — legacy, avoid beyond sandboxes), predefined (default choice, Google-maintained), custom (~300 per org and per project quota, permanent drift-maintenance burden). Predefined-first.

flashcards.q: What can IAM Conditions key on and what are the gotchas?
flashcards.a: resource.name/type/tags, request.time, sometimes origin.resource. Gotchas: expressions fail closed; time conditions don't revoke already-minted OAuth tokens; tag-based conditions break if tags change outside change control.

flashcards.q: Org Policy vs deny policy vs PAB — one line each?
flashcards.a: Org policy: deploy-time guardrail on configuration writes (boolean/list/custom CEL since 2023, dry-run supported). Deny policy: request-time hard stop on specific permissions regardless of allows, attachment at org/folder/project, exceptionPrincipals for break-glass. PAB: request-time cap on which resources a principal may touch; subtractive, partial service coverage.

flashcards.q: Three debugging tools and their questions?
flashcards.a: Policy Troubleshooter: why was this principal denied this permission on this resource (walks bindings/conditions/deny)? Policy Analyzer: who can call permission X here (expands groups + inheritance)? IAM Recommender: which roles are over-provisioned based on 90-day observed usage?

flashcards.q: Which two default service accounts exist in every project?
flashcards.a: App Engine default PROJECT_ID@appspot.gserviceaccount.com and Compute Engine default PROJECT_NUMBER-compute@developer.gserviceaccount.com. Both historically auto-granted roles/editor; newer projects skip that grant (configurable ~2024); blank SA fields still silently select them.
